description: Navigate to login via 'Login' link on onboarding carousel (OCR vision match)
Wait 2 s for login screen to fully render before injecting credentials
Tap phone field to focus it. Pixel 6 (2400x1080px, density 2.625): AppBar ~56dp + phone row centre ~248dp from body top = 304dp from safe-area = 798px physical. Screen centre x = 539px.
Wait for soft keyboard to appear

Inject phone number digits via OS-level ADB input. Bypasses Flutter accessibility tree, input formatters, and Semantics wrappers entirely. The _phoneController listener fires setState() -> _canLogin recalculates.
Dismiss keyboard with KEYCODE_ESCAPE so we can tap the password field
Wait for keyboard to fully dismiss
Tap password field. Password row centre ~352dp from body top = 432dp from safe-area = 1134px physical.

Inject password. Password is client-side only (never sent to Firebase - app uses phone OTP auth). Value meets validation rules: >=8 chars, uppercase D, lowercase evon, digits 1100. No special chars to avoid ADB shell-escaping issues with @.
Wait for Flutter controller listeners to fire setState() -> _canLogin=true -> login button onPressed enabled
Tap Log in button via OCR vision match (more reliable than coordinate tap for the button itself)
Wait 6 s for Firebase verificationCompleted auto-verify + Navigator to push /home
